paper_metadata.title: New insight for designing high-strength medium-entropy alloy with resistance to intermediate-temperature embrittlement by nitrogen-induced Ti-rich precipitation mechanism

evidence.quote: we propose the introduction of nitrogen into a lightweight TiVNb medium-entropy alloy

In the region with large orientation differences, a dispersive distribution of small HCP Ti-rich phases is retained (Fig. 4e and f, white dots).
Turbine blade-like precipitates appear in the vicinity of GBs (Fig. 2b). Each blade comprises many discontinuous lamellae (Fig. 2c).
TEM imaging demonstrates the formation of FCC twins (a = 436 pm) at the GB, which have titanium-rich composition and contain up to 8 % N, indicating that N is easily segregated at GBs (Fig. 4g).

evidence.section: 4.1. Formation mechanism of titanium-rich chain-like precipitation
evidence.quote: Therefore, it is reasonable to infer that the addition of nitrogen atoms leads to the local enrichment of titanium atoms during the quenching of the TiVNb alloy, which facilitates Ti precipitation. This process is termed ‘nitrogen-induced titanium enrichment’.

evidence.section: 4.3. Reasons for the high alloy strength
evidence.quote: This high strength can be accounted for in two ways: (1) interstitial atom strengthening and (2) discontinuous Ti-rich lamellae strengthening. Except for a small amount of nitrogen precipitated in Ti-rich phases, most nitrogen is dissolved in the BCC matrix, causing lattice distortion.

evidence.section: 4.2. Mechanisms for the elimination of intermediate-temperature brittleness
evidence.quote: indicating that turbine blade-like Ti-rich precipitates are strongly binded to the matrix and can play a role in deflecting cracks, thereby increasing the fracture energy of the material.
